_description: Task13 DRIFT field, FINE transcription -- the 0.1mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume, for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.22mm far-field grid. NOTHING IS SNAPPED HERE, which is the opposite of the coarse file: at 0.1mm every true design length is an exact whole number of cells -- pixelSize 3.5 -> 35 cells, pixelGap 0.9 -> 9, chamfer_r 0.7 -> 7 (via int(round()) in the generator; 0.7/0.1 is 6.999999999999999 in binary float, so the rounding is load-bearing). The coarse file carries the snapped 3.52 / 0.88 / 0.66 with the design values preserved as _design_* keys; here the values ARE the design values. PITCH: 3.5 + 0.9 = 4.4mm = 44 fine cells and 20 coarse cells of 0.22mm. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise. PIXEL PLANE LOW EDGE 9.9 IS LOAD-BEARING: 9.9mm is 99 fine cells AND 45 coarse cells of 0.22mm, so the pad plane lands on a real node of BOTH grids. Moving it breaks that co-location. (The generator reads this key with int(), not int(round()) -- gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py:474 -- so never reason about it in decimal; 9.9/0.1 is exactly 99.0 and 9.9/0.22 exactly 45.0 in binary float, but neighbouring values are not so lucky.) DEPTH: driftZDepth 79.15 is the electron launch node, deliberately NOT rounded to 79.2. The cathode sits on the domain's last plane at ceil(79.15/0.22) = 360 coarse cells = 79.2mm, which is 792 fine cells exactly, so both grids close on the same physical cathode; the launch node itself does not land on that grounded plane, which is the point. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition). The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. NOTE: CathodePotential -8400 was NOT re-derived when this file was retargeted from the 159.9mm depth. The drift length is now 79.15 - 9.9 = 69.25mm, so -8400 V is 121.3 V/mm nominal, not the 56.04 V/mm the old 149.9mm geometry gave. Re-derive it before running. TILE SIZE: Npixels 5, i.e. a 5x5 pad tile at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse for the weighting probe; the DRIFT field is one periodic tile, so Npixels does not size this file's domain. GridPotential does NOT enter the cathode calculation: the shield grid has holes and is transparent at the tile centre, so it is not an equipotential plane terminating the field. The bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. GridPotential instead sets the collection field between the grid and the pads.
